races.name: CopyBet Proudly Backs UK Horse Racing Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Eternal Angel
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who won over this course and distance 24 days ago; her recent two-race winning sequence on Good ground makes her the natural pace-setter, and the absence of rivals to press her is a significant structural advantage, though she is technically racing slightly out of her optimal prominent style per the fit tag.

runners_data.name: Aimeric
runners_data.note: Lightly exposed hold-up type for Jennie Candlish, arriving 40 days fresh with a form string of just two starts, both on Good; he is a genuine closer whose finishing effort depends on the front group tiring, but he will find himself racing out of his natural rear position in this compacted field.

runners_data.name: Arcon
runners_data.note: Candlish's second string carries a prior Flat win on Good ground and jumps form that includes a hurdle victory, but six of seven career starts have produced mid-to-rear finishes; his natural come-from-behind style will be squeezed into midfield here, diluting his chance unless the race unravels late.

runners_data.name: Happy Harrison
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Gary Hanmer — three runs all at 16f on Good, all placed or thereabouts — whose trainer has a cold book (0/7 over 14 days) but whose track record at this trip and going is the most consistent in the field; needs a strong pace to bring his late run into play.

runners_data.name: Ride Like A Girl
runners_data.note: Jamie Snowden's five-year-old has won twice over 2m on Good at this sort of level and her form string (1-4-4-3-1) is the most solid in the race; Gavin Sheehan takes the ride for a trainer striking at 6/17 over 14 days, and she is the most natural prominent partner to Eternal Angel in the early stages.

runners_data.name: Dancingondiamonds
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen takes the reins for Olly Murphy (4/13, 14-day strike) on this hold-up type who has just one hurdle run (8th on Good over 2m) to his name; naturally races from off the pace but the redistribution note reflects that there are too many hold-up horses here for him to find clear space, compressing his chance.

runners_data.name: Mystic Wind
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton sends out this four-year-old (Harry Skelton up, trainer on a hot 17/31 streak) on just two hurdle starts, both on Good at 2m, both finishing mid-pack; the strong trainer-jockey combination is the headline, though his hold-up style leaves him reliant on a fast early gallop that this race is unlikely to provide.

runners_data.name: Rose Warrior
runners_data.note: Third Candlish runner in the race, returning from a fall last time (43 days ago); prior hurdle form is modest — best effort a fourth on Standard — and on Good ground he has never threatened; his prominent Flat profile suggests he could slot into a handy position, but there is little evidence he can match the leaders at this level.

runners_data.name: Amalfina
runners_data.note: DJ Jeffreys' four-year-old has a flat-track base and a best hurdle effort of third on Heavy ground; her natural style is to race held up, and with this field already over-populated with closers she will struggle to find room and daylight in the straight; low weight (145lbs) is a minor positive.

runners_data.name: Pearl Knot
runners_data.note: Debutant over hurdles for Greenall/Guerriero — just one track appearance (unseated, 20f on Good, 11 days ago) — making her a genuine unknown quantity; unknown style flag is appropriate, and backers should note the recency of that run and the physical question mark that any unseating leaves.

races.paceDynamic: Eternal Angel is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival willing to press from the front, she should be able to dictate at a measured, sustainable gallop over Uttoxeter's 2m trip on Good ground. Ride Like A Girl is the most likely horse to track closely in second, given her prominent style and strong recent form over this exact course and distance, creating a compact lead group of two at most. The majority of the field — Aimeric, Arcon, Dancingondiamonds, Amalfina, Mystic Wind, Happy Harrison, Rose Warrior and Pearl Knot — are hold-up or midfield types, meaning the race will effectively split into a small group up front and a large cluster behind, with little mid-race pressure on Eternal Angel. This shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently and produce a clean jump at the last — front-running and prominent-racing profiles hold the clear structural edge. The field carries considerably more hold-up horses than can be accommodated at the back; Eternal Angel and Ride Like A Girl are most likely to actually secure their natural position, while Dancingondiamonds, Aimeric, Arcon and Amalfina are all true hold-up types who will find themselves racing out of role in a compacted midfield.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Eternal Angel Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Eternal Angel bowls along uncontested and Ride Like A Girl slots in behind without drama.
scenarios.body: Eternal Angel sets a measured pace that suits her proven front-running profile, and the absence of any genuine challenger allows her to conserve energy before quickening at the second-last; the Good ground and 2m trip are squarely in her wheelhouse based on her recent win here. Ride Like A Girl, the only other natural prominent runner, is ideally positioned to pounce if Eternal Angel flattens late but may struggle to close the gap if the leader jumps well.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swamp Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Eternal Angel sets too brisk a pace that causes her to empty, allowing the held-up pack to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: Eternal Angel, racing over-eagerly without restraint, hits a flat spot in the straight and the compact hold-up group, led by whichever of Aimeric or Mystic Wind travels best, sweeps past at the final hurdle. Aimeric, despite being redistributed in this map, is a genuine hold-up performer whose finishing kick could prove decisive if the front group obliges.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Ride Like A Girl tracks Eternal Angel closely throughout and out-stays her up the run-in.
scenarios.body: Ride Like A Girl has won twice over exactly this course and distance on Good ground and her five-race form string shows consistent form at 16f on Good, making her an ideal beneficiary if the pace is just right for a held-up tracker to reel in the leader. She can challenge at the last hurdle and use her stamina to grind past if Eternal Angel cannot accelerate again.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Race, Late Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple hold-up horses club together mid-pack and one gets a dream passage to the front at the last.
scenarios.body: With so many natural hold-up types crammed into midfield and racing out of their preferred roles, a stumble, traffic problem or early fall could compress the field and hand an opportunist a clear run late; Arcon, who has a prior win on Good ground, is the likeliest beneficiary of a chaotic finish given his trainer's in-form yard. This is a low-probability scenario dependent on significant disruption to the otherwise straightforward pace map.

watchPoints.text: Ride Like A Girl is the most obvious danger to Eternal Angel given two wins over this exact 2m trip on Good at Uttoxeter — watch whether Gavin Sheehan pushes up to track the leader from the front or elects to drop in and risk getting caught in the hold-up traffic.

The sheer volume of hold-up horses (Aimeric, Arcon, Dancingondiamonds, Amalfina, Mystic Wind) all racing out of their natural position creates a high risk of a mid-race pile-up or interference at the hurdles — watch the third hurdle where the pack typically bunches at Uttoxeter.

Mystic Wind with Harry Skelton carries the hottest trainer form in the race (Dan Skelton 17/31 over 14 days) — watch market moves close to post time, as stable confidence could indicate a step forward from two promising but unspectacular hurdle starts.

Pearl Knot is a complete wildcard having unseated just 11 days ago — watch her jumping from the first hurdle, as a novice with that recent experience could unsettle rivals if she makes a mistake at the early obstacles.

Jennie Candlish runs three horses (Aimeric, Arcon, Rose Warrior) — watch which one the market favours in the final show, as stable runners in a yard with multiple entries often have a clear stable pick that the price will reflect.

races.name: CopyBet Daily World Cup Profit Boost Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Gaelic Rambler
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse returning after 77 days off; form on Good ground is moderate (0 wins, 3 places from 7) and the lengthy absence is a concern for a trainer whose 14-day strike rate is modest at 1/18; headgear (tongue tie, cheekpieces) retained.

runners_data.name: That's Nice
runners_data.note: Nicky Henderson runner who holds good course form (two thirds on Good at 24f) and Harry Cobden is a significant booking; a genuine hold-up horse that will need a strong pace to produce a finishing effort, which Hudson's solo lead may not fully supply.

runners_data.name: Hudson
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner and likely to steal a comfortable lead on Good ground; his STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) reflects a mismatch between his natural role and the pace he creates — he sets the race up but his finishing effort under a big weight (161lbs) is questionable.

runners_data.name: Jiair Madrik
runners_data.note: Two consecutive wins on Good ground (20f and 21f) make this the most in-form horse in the field; Donald McCain's 14-day figures are solid (2/15) and the prominent style is perfectly matched to a Hudson-led race — Theo Gillard can simply track and pounce.

runners_data.name: Seeitoldya
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose true rear-of-field role has pushed it into the midfield mapping; five recent runs without a win or place and a 103-day break suggest this is the weakest profile in the race — the redistribution only adds to the tactical compromise.

runners_data.name: Back In The Bay
runners_data.note: Strong form record (2 wins, 4 places from 9 on Good) but its natural hold-up style is squeezed by the crowded rear of the field; the horse must race closer than ideal, which historically has not brought out its best, though Jonathan Burke is capable of improvising.

runners_data.name: The Clonmel Kid
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's horse has a solid record on Good ground (1 win, 4 places from 13) and carries headgear (hood); forced into a midfield position by the redistribution rather than natural preference, and at OR 103 is the lowest-rated runner — needs things to go right.

runners_data.name: Ice Jet
runners_data.note: Three consecutive wins on Good ground and Dan Skelton's yard is firing (10/30 in 14 days); Harry Skelton will want to get this horse covered up but the volume of hold-up types means it may need to race handier than ideal — if it can hold a midfield position, its class (OR 113) is a genuine threat late.

races.paceDynamic: Hudson is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with just one prominent-style horse in the field, is likely to dictate from the front at a sustainable gallop on Good ground over 2m4f at Uttoxeter — a track that suits front-runners who jump fluently and stay on. The remainder of the field is dominated by hold-up horses: Ice Jet, Seeitoldya, Back In The Bay, The Clonmel Kid, Gaelic Rambler and That's Nice are all natural rear-of-field types, while Jiair Madrik will look to press Hudson from a prominent position. The field holds more genuine hold-up types than the race map can physically place at the rear, meaning several of them — most notably Ice Jet and Back In The Bay — will be forced to race closer than ideal, compromising their natural finishing kick. A genuine, uncontested Hudson-led gallop on a fair surface creates a race that plays most naturally into the hands of the one or two horses who can track the pace from second or third and produce a sustained jumping effort, making prominent-tracking runners the primary beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hudson Leads, Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Hudson sets a controlled, uncontested gallop and a close-tracking rival jumps efficiently to pounce from the second-last fence.
scenarios.body: Hudson's lone front-running role creates a genuine target for any horse that can hold a prominent position through the race — Jiair Madrik is perfectly placed as the natural tracker, with two recent wins on Good ground confirming suitability for exactly this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Late
scenarios.trigger: If Hudson sets a falsely slow tempo that compresses the field and allows genuine hold-up horses to produce a late burst from the final fence.
scenarios.body: A dawdle would allow the deeper hold-up horses — Gaelic Rambler and That's Nice — to close from further back, with the run-in at Uttoxeter giving them time to pick up; That's Nice carries strong handler form at the track and Cobden's experience is a factor.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Hudson jumps boldly and presses on from the home turn, building an unassailable lead that the hold-up horses simply cannot reel in.
scenarios.body: On Good ground with no rival pressing him, Hudson can dictate every stride and his jumping accuracy becomes decisive; the field's hold-up bias means few rivals will have the momentum to close over the final two fences.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Fallers Reshape Race
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors, a fall or unseating among the prominent horses scrambles the expected shape and reshuffles the running order dramatically.
scenarios.body: Hudson's fall or blunder would instantly create a new contest among the hold-up horses forced into the front, favouring whichever improver can adapt quickest; Ice Jet's rapid recent progression (three consecutive wins) gives it the class to handle a muddled scenario.

watchPoints.text: Hudson jumps the first two fences cleanly — if he misses one early he may be headed before the field settles and the entire race shape changes.

Ice Jet is being pushed out of its natural hold-up role by field congestion; watch whether Skelton allows it to drift back naturally or accepts a more prominent position — this tactical call will define its chance.

Jiair Madrik's two recent wins came at 20f and 21f; this is 24f (2m4f) and there is a stamina question at this longer trip on a fair-going chase track — watch its jumping and jumping rhythm in the back straight.

Back In The Bay has strong form on Good ground but the redistribution forces Jonathan Burke to race closer than the horse prefers; if it gets trapped in traffic behind Hudson, its late finishing effort may be blunted.

Uttoxeter's run-in is relatively short after the final fence, favouring horses that have delivered their effort by the second-last — horses held up very late (Gaelic Rambler, Seeitoldya) may simply not have enough real estate to finish.

races.name: Peter Smith Birthday Celebration Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Karnaval Point
runners_data.note: Won twice over 20f on Good ground in recent form (form: 461-13) and David Pipe's six-year-old faces the lightest possible task at the head of affairs here; the sole genuine front-runner in the field, his STYLE_FIT flag is irrelevant in a race he will likely lead throughout, and the 33-day break looks fine.|

runners_data.name: Ivane
runners_data.note: James Owen's eight-year-old carries a visor and has a solid Good-ground record (sim-going 9/15, 3W7P) but his OR-117 best form has come at distances shorter than today's 3m — Jonathan Burke takes over and the horse will want to push forward despite being surrounded by other prominent types competing for the same ground.|

runners_data.name: Paper Mill
runners_data.note: Stuart Edmunds' ten-year-old won over 26f on Soft recently but a 164-day layoff is a major concern at this level; Charlie Hammond's mount is a front-runner by nature yet the glut of prominent horses means he is likely to find himself racing off the pace against his instincts, and his T14 blank (0/10) adds further caution.|

runners_data.name: Fairlawn Flyer
runners_data.note: The most recent runner in the field (11 days), Mickey Bowen's ten-year-old has solid Good-ground chase form (sim-going 7/15, 2W4P) and Mr James Murray's 7lb claim is useful — he genuinely wants to race prominently and has the course-fit edge, but racing off the pace if unable to secure his position would blunt his chance considerably.|

runners_data.name: Eaton Anne
runners_data.note: Olly Murphy's eight-year-old carries tongue-tie and visor and boasts solid placed form (2nd twice on Soft, 2nd on Good recently), with Sean Bowen an obvious positive; a front-runner by inclination who has been pushed to the rear of the map by the prominent traffic ahead of her — if she can work forward early she is more dangerous than her forced position suggests.|

runners_data.name: A Dublin Job
runners_data.note: Sarah-Jayne Davies' nine-year-old has a strong Good-ground record (sim-going 11/15, 3W5P) with wins at 20-22f, but today's 3m looks a stretch beyond his optimum trip; James Best partners a horse who naturally races up with the pace yet will likely find himself further back than ideal given the crowded prominent group, and the T14 blank (0/5) is a negative flag.|

races.paceDynamic: Karnaval Point is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner 3m chase and should bowl along at a sustainable, uncontested gallop from the off — David Pipe's six-year-old has the pace profile to dictate entirely on his own terms on Good ground at Uttoxeter. Behind him, every other runner in the field is a natural prominent racer: Ivane, Paper Mill, Fairlawn Flyer, A Dublin Job, and Eaton Anne all want to race up with the pace, meaning the map has been forced to redistribute several of them into midfield and hold-up positions that do not reflect their true style. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can physically accommodate — of the prominent brigade, Ivane (OR 117, Sean Bowen's mount Eaton Anne) and Fairlawn Flyer (course-fit, recent run 11 days ago) are best placed to actually secure their natural position close to Karnaval Point, while Paper Mill, A Dublin Job, and Eaton Anne will likely find themselves held up against their will. The tactical verdict is clear: a controlled, uncontested lead for Karnaval Point at a genuine 3m chase gallop over Good ground strongly favours horses that can travel prominently in behind before asserting — patient prominent racers with strong Good-ground records hold the structural edge here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Karnaval Point Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Karnaval Point bowls along uncontested and sets a fair but not suicidal gallop, dictating the race from flag to near-finish.
scenarios.body: He is alone in front, faces zero pressure on Good ground over a trip he has won at, and his prominent challengers are bunched in behind unable to work their way into contention early enough. Horses who can travel smoothly in the slipstream before delivering a clean challenge two out are the prime beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Push Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Ivane or Fairlawn Flyer refuse to settle and push up to challenge Karnaval Point, ratcheting the tempo across the 3m trip.
scenarios.body: A contested front makes this a genuine stamina test on Good ground, and the extra distance plus increased gallop will sort the field on class and fitness. Runners with proven Good-ground staying form and a clean recent prep — particularly those with the OR and a genuine 3m record — become the clear threats.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Chaos Thins Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses mid-race through a faller or departures, leaving a small, tactical finish from the last fence.
scenarios.body: A reduced field with a slow tempo invites a sprint finish, which would benefit any runner with a high TS and the ability to quicken late — but given almost every horse here is a prominent type rather than a true closer, this scenario is inherently unreliable and the form book advantage is hard to assign cleanly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves genuinely strong enough to crack the front-runners, leaving room for hold-up horses to sweep past.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires horses mapped to the rear to act as genuine closers — but Eaton Anne and A Dublin Job are natural prominent racers redistributed to hold-up positions, meaning they are not true late finishers and this shape is structurally unlikely to materialise as intended.

watchPoints.text: Fairlawn Flyer and Ivane — both are genuine prominent types and the most likely to push up and contest the lead with Karnaval Point; if either forces the pace from the front, the gallop materially increases and the race shape shifts from controlled to contested.|

Paper Mill's 164-day absence — Stuart Edmunds' ten-year-old has had no racecourse outing since early in the year, and at 3m on Good ground with a crowded prominent group ahead of him, he may not find his feet quickly enough to factor.|

Eaton Anne racing against type — Sean Bowen's mount is naturally front-running but has been forced to the rear of the field map; watch for Bowen attempting to push forward from the off, which could trigger early jostling for position and disrupt the anticipated clean breakaway by Karnaval Point.|

A Dublin Job's trip stamina — his five-run good-ground history tops out at 22f and today's 3m is a career-longest test; James Best will need to conserve energy early but the horse's natural prominent style makes that tactically difficult in this particular field.|

races.name: CopyBet Support Safer Gambling Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Roger Pol
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old who has won twice over 24f on Good ground and returns from 43 days off under a 5lb claimer; his OR of 128 is the highest in the field but he is running out of his natural prominent role as a confirmed front-runner and that style-fit discount is real over this extra trip.|

runners_data.name: Sunray Shadow
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton rides a horse who has won five of his last six starts including three consecutive hurdling wins, all on Good ground, making him the form pick of the race; Dan Skelton's yard is firing at 52% over 14 days and this seven-year-old's sim-going record of 5W from 12 Good-ground runs is outstanding.|

runners_data.name: Lipa K
runners_data.note: Jack Tudor takes over on a mare with three wins from five Good-ground runs at this sort of trip; she flopped on her most recent start (9th on Good) but had won back-to-back before that and Oliver Greenall's yard is 8/26 over the fortnight — a bounce-back candidate with genuine claims.|

runners_data.name: Ernest Gray
runners_data.note: Tom Bellamy partner returns after 94 days off for Alan King; his Good-ground record reads 2W3P from six runs but his last two outings both produced sixth-place finishes and his sim-going score (6/15) is modest — freshness could help but recent form does not inspire confidence.|

runners_data.name: Smugglers Haven
runners_data.note: In-form mare who won most recently 44 days ago and has four wins from eleven on Good ground — the strongest record of any redistributed horse here; though her natural style is prominent, she was squeezed into midfield by the field's depth and Miss Lily Bradstock's 7lb claim does not fully compensate.|

runners_data.name: Champagne Twist
runners_data.note: Returned to form with a second on Good ground 48 days ago after a string of pulled-up runs; Ben Pauling's 1/13 14-day strike rate is lukewarm and his sim-going score (5/15) is the lowest of the prominent contingent — a true front-runner likely to find himself further back than ideal.|

runners_data.name: Stumps Or Slips
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen rides a nine-year-old with a remarkable sim-going record of 15/15 on Good ground, winning six of them; he has won his last three starts including back-to-back 24f victories and is the most consistent horse in the field at this trip under these conditions.|

runners_data.name: Maghlaak
runners_data.note: Returning from a 193-day absence (last run included a fall) for Mark Walford; his one win came on Soft and his Good-ground record is limited — the hold-up style and the long layoff make him a significant risk in a race that is unlikely to produce the strong gallop he needs.|

runners_data.name: Abbey Scope
runners_data.note: Nicky Richards six-year-old who has won his last two starts on Good ground at 21f and 24f; despite the redistribution into midfield away from his natural prominent role, his form figures are the most exciting in the field and Danny McMenamin is an accomplished handler.|

runners_data.name: Jet Of Magic
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old returning from 202 days off with a modest recent form string of 22/P6; his one win in the last 15 came on Soft and he is held up from a position that suits him on paper but the absence and form make him vulnerable in this company.|

runners_data.name: Hillview
runners_data.note: Benjamin Macey's 5lb claimer partners a ten-year-old whose last six runs have produced three midfield finishes and two pulls-up; his sim-going record (3W7P from 15 Good runs) is reasonable but his recent form string reads 4P7-7 and there is little to encourage.|

runners_data.name: Dr Seb
runners_data.note: Olly Murphy's nine-year-old won back-to-back on Good over 24f two runs ago but has been beaten out of sight in both subsequent starts; a natural front-runner pushed into midfield by the field's shape, and his Good-ground sim score (4/9) does not fully offset the style-fit concern at OR 108.|

races.paceDynamic: Roger Pol is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with no identified rival willing to go with him from the off, he should be able to dictate a measured, sustainable gallop over this 2m7½f trip on Good ground at Uttoxeter. Sunray Shadow, Lipa K, Ernest Gray and Stumps Or Slips are all genuine prominent types who will push forward and create a competitive early order, but with Roger Pol holding the lead comfortably, the pace is unlikely to be truly searching. This field holds more prominent-running types than can realistically secure their favoured position — Smugglers Haven, Champagne Twist, Abbey Scope and Dr Seb are all natural front-rankers who are likely to be shuffled back into a midfield they would not normally occupy, compromising their chances in this shape. A controlled, honest gallop over a thorough staying trip on sound ground plays directly into the hands of genuinely prominent-to-lead types who can travel close to the pace without expending excessive early energy, and the horses best placed to exploit that shape are those who can race in the first four without being pressured into doing so.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead Pays Off
scenarios.trigger: If Roger Pol dictates a measured tempo unchallenged and the prominent chasers drain each other's petrol settling positions behind him.
scenarios.body: Roger Pol sets a comfortable gallop, the genuine prominent types like Sunray Shadow and Stumps Or Slips track him closely and one of them has enough in reserve to overhaul him late; horses who travel well in the first three places get first run and the staying trip suits those with a clean jumping record. This shape rewards horses with high sim-going scores at this trip and the ability to switch off behind a slow-to-moderate pace before producing a sustained challenge from two out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Collide
scenarios.trigger: If the compressed prominent group jostles for positions early and the pace becomes stronger than expected, burning out the front-rank horses.
scenarios.body: With Sunray Shadow, Lipa K, Ernest Gray and Stumps Or Slips all reluctant to cede ground, the early sectionals quicken more than Roger Pol intends, creating a more truly-run race that stretches the field and suits those travelling economically just off the pressure. A horse like Stumps Or Slips, who has won five of his last fifteen on Good ground with a faultless recent record, is perfectly equipped to absorb that early battle and emerge strongest in the home straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group sets a genuinely hot gallop and the field strings out, leaving a genuine hold-up horse to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: Maghlaak or Jet Of Magic, sitting well off the pace, could find the front rank weakening from three out if the race is run at an uncharacteristically strong tempo, though neither carries a convincing recent form profile at this trip or in this going. This scenario is tempered by the fact that the horses most likely to benefit from a strong gallop are true hold-up types, and Maghlaak's 193-day absence and limited Good-ground record reduces the probability further.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Horse Defies Mapping
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent types forced into a midfield position manages to recover their natural front-rank berth and produces a career-best display.
scenarios.body: Smugglers Haven, with four wins from eleven on Good ground and a recent winning return, is the most likely of the displaced prominent types to carve out a forward position if gaps appear early; however, being out of their natural running role in a field this deep is a genuine performance constraint, and the style-fit tags across Champagne Twist, Abbey Scope and Dr Seb collectively reduce the probability of any one of them defying the race shape. This remains the lowest-probability scenario precisely because it requires horses to race against their redistributed position.

watchPoints.text: Stumps Or Slips has a 15/15 sim-going record on Good and has won his last three starts — watch whether Sean Bowen can tuck him in just behind the leaders and produce him fresh at the last two hurdles.
Sunray Shadow's five-win streak and elite trainer-jockey combination make him the most dangerous horse in the race if Harry Skelton can settle him in second or third early on.

Roger Pol sets the pace but is carrying 168lbs under a claimer over a longer trip than his recent wins — watch for any sign of the gallop quickening as the prominent group compresses behind him turning for home.

Abbey Scope's two recent wins look outstanding for his OR of 113 but he is unlikely to be able to boss from the front in this field — watch whether McMenamin can find a prominent position anyway or if he is buried in midfield.

Maghlaak's 193-day absence and Jet Of Magic's 202-day layoff mean both hold-up horses are essentially unknown quantities returning cold — if either is rusty early the hold-up scenario probability drops further.

races.name: CopyBet Pay First Past The Post Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Rocks Up Late
runners_data.note: Won on Good over this exact course and distance last time out; Ben Pauling's runner has 5 wins or places from 6 Good-ground starts and handles this trip well, but the STYLE_FIT flag is a genuine caveat — it is mapped as Prominent yet its data tag suggests it may not fully reproduce that role, so treat with mild caution despite the strong recent form.

runners_data.name: Jammy Jay
runners_data.note: 173 days off the track is a significant concern for Charlie Deutsch's mount; ran on soft ground last twice and his Good-ground record is modest, and as a genuine hold-up type returning from a long break, he needs everything to fall right to be competitive.

runners_data.name: Iolaos Du Mou
runners_data.note: Two wins on Good ground at 16f make Tabitha Worsley's mount the most authentic closer in the race; headgear (hood) is retained and the trainer strike rate is modest, but the sim-going record of 12 from 14 is the best in the field and the style fits a truly run race.

runners_data.name: Network Rgb
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen is a major positive on a 3-year-old making what appears to be a hurdling debut after a 198-day absence; all three runs have been on Soft ground, so the step up to Good is an unknown, and this is a very open profile at present.

runners_data.name: Buxted Reel
runners_data.note: Stan Sheppard's mount has a decent recent run two weeks ago and has placed twice on Good ground at 16f; a natural prominent runner whose best form has come on Easier ground, and the drop back from 20f trips to 2m here is worth noting as a potential positive.

runners_data.name: Tara Iti
runners_data.note: Headgear (visor) worn and genuinely held up in style, but the redistribution flag means it is very unlikely to get its natural rearward pitch in this field — James Best rides and the recent form string of 656P-7 is uninspiring even if it finds cleaner air.

runners_data.name: Colinski
runners_data.note: The 3lb claim from Charlie Maggs is a small positive for Rebecca Menzies' 4-year-old; a true hold-up horse whose natural style is compromised by the crowded rear of field, and only three career runs means the profile is still thin — the one Good-ground placing at this trip is encouraging but the redistribution limits realistic expectations.

runners_data.name: Huit Reflets
runners_data.note: Mark Walford's 9-year-old has been running well in placing form at 20f on Soft; the drop back to 2m on Good is a double shift in conditions that may not suit, and while prominent in style, the best of his recent form has come at longer trips in deeper ground.

runners_data.name: Cawthorne Banker
runners_data.note: Jonjo O'Neill Jr takes over the ride and the horse has placed on Good ground at 16f as recently as 20 days ago; genuine hold-up ability is present in the form, but the out-of-role mapping means it will likely race closer than ideal — the b-headgear is retained and the course form is relevant.

runners_data.name: Genbu
runners_data.note: Sarah-Jayne Davies' 4-year-old has been remarkably consistent on Good ground at 16f with two wins and five places from nine sim-going starts; a natural prominent racer whose style fits this race shape well, and the improving profile of a young horse could see it competitive at a favourable weight.

runners_data.name: Whatcombe
runners_data.note: Ben Poste partners a lightly-raced 4-year-old for Faye Bramley who has never won on record and whose last run at 16f on Good saw an 11th-place finish; the redistribution means it races closer than its natural rear-of-field tendency, and the 0W0P sim-going record is the most modest in the field.

races.paceDynamic: Rocks Up Late is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should be able to stride into a comfortable, uncontested rhythm from the outset on Good ground at Uttoxeter over 2m. Buxted Reel and Huit Reflets are the likeliest horses to press from a prominent position, but neither is a natural front-runner, so the pace Rocks Up Late sets is unlikely to be pressured into being falsely fast. The result is a race run at a sustainable, honest gallop that will not shred the field — giving the lead horse a genuine chance to control tempo and potentially steal a march turning in. This shape strongly favours hold-up horses with a turn of foot and prominent racers who can travel within themselves, but critically, Colinski, Tara Iti, Cawthorne Banker, and Whatcombe are all true hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map because this field contains more horses wanting to race at the rear than there is room for — those most likely to actually secure a rearward pitch are Cawthorne Banker, who has shown genuine hold-up ability at this trip and going, and Iolaos Du Mou, whose natural style and course form make it the most authentic closer in the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rocks Up Late Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Rocks Up Late is allowed to bowl along at a comfortable pace unchallenged and the field settles tamely behind.
scenarios.body: Rocks Up Late dictates from the front, the pace remains steady without burning off the prominent runners, and the race becomes a test of jumping and class rather than stamina — Rocks Up Late's recent Goodish-ground form and OR 98 make it hard to peg back. Prominent types who travel smoothly into the race without being asked questions early are the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Arrive Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and the field strings out, allowing genuine hold-up horses to pick up ground in the straight.
scenarios.body: Iolaos Du Mou and Cawthorne Banker, as the most authentic hold-up runners, would be best placed to exploit tired horses if the early gallop proves more taxing than anticipated. Iolaos Du Mou's two wins on Good ground at 2m and strong sim-going record make it the standout closer if this scenario materialises.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is moderate and a prominent chaser tracks Rocks Up Late closely enough to deliver a challenge at the final hurdle.
scenarios.body: Genbu has shown consistent prominence-style form on Good ground at 2m, winning at the trip and placing repeatedly, and is well-suited to a race where sitting just off the pace allows a smooth jump at the last. Huit Reflets and Buxted Reel also fit this mould, though both carry more exposed profiles at this level.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Fades, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Rocks Up Late is pressed earlier than expected and the moderate pace collapses, creating a messy finish with multiple horses in contention.
scenarios.body: A bunched finish on the flat after the last hurdle could see any of the redistributed midfield types get involved if they find a seam, but the out-of-role nature of Tara Iti, Colinski, and Whatcombe in these positions means they are unlikely to be optimally placed. Network Rgb, the youngest horse in the field returning from 198 days off, is a wildcard if Olly Murphy has it tuned up.

watchPoints.text: Rocks Up Late jumping fluently at the second and third hurdles — if it gets into a comfortable rhythm uncontested, it could build a lead that proves very difficult to close down on Good ground at 2m.

Monitor how many of the true hold-up horses (Cawthorne Banker, Colinski, Tara Iti, Whatcombe) are forced to race closer than ideal in the first half-mile — a bunched midfield group racing out of style could compromise their runs and distort the finish.

Network Rgb is unknown on Good ground after three Soft-ground runs and 198 days off; Sean Bowen will have the horse fit but a big run first time back and on a different surface would be a surprise — any drift in the market should be noted.

Iolaos Du Mou's jumping — as the most authentic closer, it needs clean jumping and a smooth passage through the field; any early errors at the hurdles will cost it ground it cannot afford to give away with the pace unlikely to be truly strong.

Genbu's sectional position at halfway — if Charlie Price settles it just off the prominent group rather than being drawn wide, the consistent Good-ground form at this trip gives it a live chance of picking up the pieces if Rocks Up Late is reeled in late.

runners_data.name: Alshadhian
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse with a strong record in similar Good-ground 2m chases (8 runs, 1W6P), trained by Greenall & Guerriero who are 0/3 in the last 14 days; the tight headgear (hg:t) suggests he needs plenty of driving, and Jack Tudor's positive riding style is an asset in a slowly-run race where position off the final bend is critical.

runners_data.name: Person Of Interest
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden takes the ride for an in-form Faye Bramley yard (3W from last 6, T14), which is the headline angle here; true hold-up operator whose form string of P49-U6 is mixed but he has finished in the first four on Good ground 3 of 5 times, and the 20-day turnaround suits a fit horse.

runners_data.name: Electric Eddy
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed pace-setter who will lead from the start at a sustainable gallop — at OR 94 he is well-handicapped if he dictates, but the STYLE_FIT tag (0.92) is relevant only if he is somehow not allowed to stride on; Twiston-Davies yard is 0/8 in the last 14 days, which is a minor negative around what is otherwise a straightforward positional play.

runners_data.name: Most Wanted
runners_data.note: Won last time out (1/16f/GOO) at the same trip and surface, making him the form horse in the race; he carries headgear (hg:p) and has a solid Good-ground record (2W4P from 12 runs), and Brendan Powell can be enterprising — the 37-day break is the only query but he looks fit enough to figure.

runners_data.name: Feet On The Ground
runners_data.note: Fergal O'Brien's yard is active (3/20 in T14) and this horse has the profile of a track specialist, but his true style is hold-up and he has been pushed into a midfield slot because the rear is overcrowded; his sim-going record is modest (0W2P from 5 relevant runs) and the STYLE_FIT discount applies — he is best watched rather than relied upon unless he genuinely secures a prominent early position.

runners_data.name: Royal Rhythm
runners_data.note: A 10-year-old veteran who has finished fifth in five of his last six runs — consistent but not a winner, and his sim-going record (0W2P) on Good reflects that; Jonjo O'Neill Jr provides some upside, but this horse's natural tendency to sit deep means he is unlikely to achieve the midfield pitch the map assigns him, making him a tough win proposition.

runners_data.name: Fond Farewell
runners_data.note: Form reads /UP-54, with falls and unseats punctuating his record — jumping reliability is the key question here for a horse whose best Going figures come on soft ground (hg:t again suggests he needs encouragement); mapped to midfield due to overcrowding at the rear but his authentic finishing style means he is best suited to a truly run race, which this is not.

runners_data.name: Prairie Queen
runners_data.note: Lightly weighted at OR 77 but in excellent recent form (233-13), with a win 20 days ago at the same distance on Good ground; her sim-going record is outstanding (1W8P from 14 runs on similar Going) and Sean Houlihan's claim brings her weight right down — the redistribution away from her natural hold-up spot is the tactical uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Walk The Plank
runners_data.note: Won over course and distance (1/16f/GOO) earlier in the season, giving him genuine place claims on an unchanged surface; Dylan Johnston is a capable young rider but the horse's form since that win (4th, 5th) suggests he may need things to fall right, and his STYLE_FIT tag (0.91) means he is unlikely to reproduce that win from a forced midfield position.

runners_data.name: Getaway Jewel
runners_data.note: At 12 years old, Brian Hughes takes the ride for Micky Hammond (1/7 T14), and the veteran did finish 2nd and 3rd in his last two starts on Good ground; he is a true hold-up horse pushed into a midfield slot, his overall form is declining with age, and he is best treated as an each-way outsider in a scenario where the race develops very late.

races.paceDynamic: Electric Eddy is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner 2m handicap chase at Uttoxeter on Good ground, and with no other natural pace-setter to challenge, he is set to dictate from the front at a sustainable, uncontested tempo. Behind him, the vast majority of this field — Alshadhian, Person Of Interest, Most Wanted, Feet On The Ground, Royal Rhythm, Fond Farewell, Prairie Queen, Walk The Plank and Getaway Jewel — are all hold-up or come-from-behind types, meaning the race will be strung out in a single-file procession behind one leader. This creates a classic setup where Electric Eddy controls fractions, jumps out to a clear advantage, and the closers must reel him in across the final two fences without ever truly disrupting his rhythm. The race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with a sharp turn of foot and a proven record on Good ground at this sort of trip, as the steady pace means stamina will not be fully tested and the race will be decided in the final half-mile. The field holds far more true hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — those most likely to actually secure a prominent pitch close to Electric Eddy are Feet On The Ground and Royal Rhythm, both redistributed from their natural deep position into a midfield slot they may not naturally achieve.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Electric Eddy Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Electric Eddy bowls along in front at a controlled tempo and the hold-up horses fail to close the gap in time.
scenarios.body: Electric Eddy dictates every yard at a steady gallop, jumps cleanly, and his rivals can never generate enough momentum off the slow pace to reel him in; the lack of a genuine pressing pace turns the race into a time-trial he sets himself. Horses with finishing pace who can travel smoothly in behind and pounce at the last two fences benefit most — Most Wanted and Prairie Queen, both proven on Good ground at 2m, are best placed to challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closer Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace set by Electric Eddy is just strong enough to stretch the field and a genuine hold-up horse produces a sustained run from the final bend.
scenarios.body: A true hold-up horse who has been biding time in mid-to-rear delivers a powerful late run as Electric Eddy's advantage diminishes after the last; this is the scenario that suits the deeper closers whose natural position at the rear is authentic. Alshadhian and Person Of Interest, both carrying strong Good-ground form, have the profiles to produce that kind of late surge if the tempo is honest enough.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed horses — Feet On The Ground, Royal Rhythm — do manage to secure a closer pitch and use that proximity to win the jumping battle.
scenarios.body: Feet On The Ground or Royal Rhythm tracks Electric Eddy just off the pace and uses that better jumping position to pounce before the true hold-up horses can fire; however, both carry STYLE_FIT discounts and neither has a strong winning record on this Going at this trip. The probability is tempered by the fact that this outcome depends on horses racing out of their natural role in a race shape that doesn't demand it.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Shock Result/Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Electric Eddy makes a costly jumping error or falls, fragmenting the race and turning it into a rough, attritional scramble.
scenarios.body: Without the controlling pace-setter the race breaks up into a messy, uneven contest where jumping errors multiply on Good ground and the most resolute stayer prevails; Walk The Plank and Getaway Jewel, both with course-relevant form and proven ability to grind out results in open races, could sneak through the carnage. This is a low-probability tail risk but merits acknowledgement given Electric Eddy's age and the chaotic dynamics that would follow his exit.

watchPoints.text: Electric Eddy sets every meaningful pace parameter in this race — if he jumps cleanly and leads unchallenged throughout, he makes the shape entirely predictable and all outcomes flow from whether the field can close, so watch his jumping from the off.

Most Wanted arrives here as the form horse having won last time out at the same course, distance and going — if he travels smoothly in behind Electric Eddy, he is the single biggest threat to upset the pace-setter late and his headgear (hood/p) suggests he switches on quickly.

Prairie Queen is significantly well-in at OR 77 with a recent win and outstanding sim-going figures (14/15 runs on similar ground) — the combination of Sean Houlihan's claim and current form makes her a potential improver who could be missed at a big price.

The redistributed cluster of Feet On The Ground, Royal Rhythm, Fond Farewell, Walk The Plank and Getaway Jewel all want to race from the rear but cannot all do so — watch the early stages to see which of them settles furthest back and whether any manage to get a genuine prominent pitch, as that will materially change the race picture.

Jonjo O'Neill Jr on Royal Rhythm and Harry Cobden on Person Of Interest are both senior jockeys on hold-up horses — if either makes an atypically forward move early to avoid getting trapped behind the crowd, it could trigger a rush for position that briefly tests Electric Eddy's lead before he settles.
